PullRequest.Title: Fix Multi Diff debug command in Agents window
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- expose the existing Multi Diff layout debug command in the Agents Window Command Palette while the single-pane Changes editor is active
- reuse the shared command ID and localized title without weakening its normal workbench precondition
- add a regression test for the Sessions-owned palette contribution

## Testing

- `changesViewActions.test.ts`: 13 passed
- pre-commit hygiene checks passed

Scenarios.Scenario: Sessions/Agents window startup and Changes contribution registration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Sessions startup imports the multi-diff contribution before the Changes contribution; both complete during module evaluation before the relevant editor and command registrations are available.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One module evaluation and one command-palette menu contribution per window startup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous module registration; no queue, fan-out, or concurrent work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ES module loading is cached. The newly referenced actions module is already imported and evaluated through multiDiffEditor.contribution.js earlier in sessions.common.main.ts, so the later import resolves from the module cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: sessions.common.main.ts imports multiDiffEditor.contribution.js before changes.contribution.js, and the former already imports actions.js and registers the action.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact module-loader timings are not measured, but the import order proves no additional actions-module evaluation or transitive loading in this product entry point.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Static ID/title extraction preserves one-time action initialization, and the added import does not expand startup module evaluation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Command Palette while the single-pane Session Changes editor is active
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Palette construction reads the command-palette registry, evaluates context expressions, and filters/ranks commands before display.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total registered command/menu count. For this command, the explicit item replaces the prior implicit command-palette item because _appendImplicitItems deduplicates by command ID, so effective command cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous menu enumeration and context evaluation on the palette-open path; no asynchronous fan-out or added concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The menu registry is long-lived and statically populated. There is no new cache, invalidation loop, or repeated registration; one explicit item is added at module initialization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: MenuRegistry.getMenuItems seeds a command-ID set from explicit items before appending implicit commands, directly proving deduplication.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact total palette size varies by product configuration, but this diff does not increase the effective number of displayed command records for the shared ID.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change adds one simple context expression but keeps command cardinality constant and introduces no scaling boundary or meaningful repeated work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run Open Multi Diff Editor Layout Debug State from a single-pane Session Changes editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The explicit developer command synchronously snapshots and JSON-serializes layout state into an in-memory text model, then awaits opening that model in a side editor. Subsequent observable layout updates append JSON patch lines off the initial command-completion critical path while the model remains open.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.stringify of the initial layout snapshot and later JSON patch records into an in-memory text model
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once on explicit invocation, then once per non-empty layout-state patch while the debug model is alive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same action and debug-model implementation already performed this work for supported multi-diff editors; the diff only contributes the existing command ID to an additional command-palette context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial serialization is on command execution; subsequent serialization occurs during layout-state updates and is not required for normal editor progress unless the developer has explicitly opened diagnostics.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One initial snapshot per explicit invocation, followed by one patch computation/serialization per distinct layout-state update over the lifetime of the debug model; state size scales with the multi-diff layout representation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The initial model creation is synchronous and editor opening is awaited; later autorun updates are serialized through the observable/model update path with no concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. The model and autorun are disposed when the in-memory debug model is disposed; retained log text intentionally lasts for the open diagnostic editor lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the action call path, JSON serialization, autorun lifecycle, and model disposal are directly visible in the repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Layout-state update frequency and how long a developer leaves the diagnostic model open vary, but this is an explicit developer-only diagnostic workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Although the diagnostic model can grow with updates, that mechanism is pre-existing and intentional; the changed line merely exposes the existing developer command in the requested Session Changes context, which does not establish a diff-introduced performance regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all changed files and traced startup registration, command-palette enumeration, and debug-command execution. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not itself fix a proven shipped performance regression.
